title: See where the space went
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C3: each folder's share of its parent is shown: partial
C4: a folder tree the person sees: missing
C5: work down from the drive to the folder using the space (drill-down): missing
C6: store is readable by the window after the scan (prerequisite for the tree): partial
live-tree-refresh-with-100k-expanded-no-stall: Stand-in tree (none built): refresh median 84 ms (bar 50), UI gap 866 ms (bar 250), scroll jumps

mid-scan-shares-never-exceed-parent: needs first: A read path that gives the tree consistent rolled-up totals for levels 1-4 while the scan runs. Either the scanner thread publishes immutable per-folder snapshots (an extension of TopLev…
Expandable tree versus a flat drill-down list. The FolderSizes page cited describes both shapes. The proposal takes the tree so the path from the drive stays in view.
Files shown as rows next to folders, versus folders only. Row 5's own check opens a folder of 100,000 files, which is why files are rows here.
FolderTreeRowText as its own class versus formatting properties on FolderTreeNode. This is layering, and nothing in the rules depends on it.
A nonzero share that rounds to zero shows '0.0 %' (matches a hand-computed check) versus '<0.1 %' (more honest to the person). The proposal keeps '0.0 %'.
Rows reorder at hand-off from the live flat list (by bytes) to the tree (by on-disk), versus re-sorting the live list by on-disk now. Left alone, since no owed row covers the mid-scan list.

The design's Case D re-run of the StallRig network cases (N-001..N-004) on this build. They create and remove SMB client mappings on this machine, which I may not change, and the m7 decision moved row 6's new steps into a hook-driven case (T-005). The person's network pass is now stale (MainWindow.xaml(.cs), the hook and WindowCases.ps1 are on the staleness list).

Core counting finding: a sparse file written length-first (extended, then data written into the hole) keeps AllocationSize 0 in its directory entry while NTFS has 64 KiB allocated. Seen here also after a rename and after a length-changing reopen; data-first entries were current. SizeProbe trusts the listing for sparse files, so the store charged 3 of 4 such files 0 bytes on disk. That touches the 'space it actually takes on disk' counting rule and belongs to a scanner slice (e.g. probe sparse files whose listing says 0 allocated).

At the default 880x620 window the tree gets a 39 px viewport (about two rows), 43 px at the minimum size, and 134 px in a 1,000 px window. It keeps SL-040's quarter of the height beside the outcome panel. Revisit SL-040's 3:1 split or the default size now that the tree is the main result.
Person-run network pass: WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork plus Core.Tests with Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, because this slice makes the last pass stale.

Re-measure the 1 GiB budget end to end with the as-built tree. The go spike used a stand-in tree layer. Include a drive-scale scan, a large folder opened, and a second scan started over it, to confirm one store in memory at scale (T-004 proves collectability on small stores).

Add WindowMutants entries for the new cases so their ability to fail is re-provable. Suggested: the numpad * handler unwired (checked by hand this build), IsExpanded not bound to the row (T-002), and rows holding the store instead of the session (T-004).

When a live tree is built on a Core read path (per-folder snapshots or seqlock/epoch), retire TopLevelTracker and lift the 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore' rule on purpose, as docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md records.
